about_the_game:
Step into Fracturefront, a fantasy-themed third-person 3D action roguelike. At its core lies randomized equipment, forging combat that's dynamic and rich in strategic depth. You play as a warrior traversing the rifts to prevent enemies from seizing the energy core. Each journey, from barren deserts to technological planets, is a life-or-death gamble. Across dimensions, face off against manipulated monstrosities and the malevolent Lord Chaos.

▶ Explore Multiversal Worlds

Explore diverse, perilous realms and face off against ever-evolving foes and colossal behemoth bosses!

Journey through uniquely themed dimensions: from desolate ruins and gloom-shrouded forests to a cruel mechanical metropolis... Encounter a wild cast of enemies:

  • Grooving little zombies lost in the beat

  • A music-obsessed chubby fellow (Warning: Interrupt his headphones at your peril!)

  • A badass biker babe roaring on her ride

A menagerie of cute-yet-ugly weird little monsters

▶ Play Your Way

The game features multiple playable characters, each with unique classes for you to choose from.

Choose from a variety of characters, each a unique force that bends the rules of reality.

“These aren’t classes—they’re variables in a system on the brink.”

▶ Customize Your Journey

Gear System – Collect fragments of energy cores from different worlds to craft powerful new equipment.

Weapon Crafting – Build weapons using parts dropped by enemies across dimensions.

Companion System – Tap into the shattered power of broken altars to forge your ultimate support allies.

▶ Epic Boss Fights & Branching Endings

Face off against the Dimension Reaper, Kaos, a villain who manipulates rifts to devour entire worlds.

Multi-phase Boss Battles – Kaos summons echoes of fallen worlds and uses powerful skills like rift teleportation and energy siphoning.

Moral Choices, Multiple Endings – After defeating Kaos, your final decision—to destroy or preserve the energy core—will shape the fate of all worlds: will you revive the multiverse, seize power, or trap reality in an endless loop?
